title: Today’s GlusterFS Rolling Release: DHT Lock Cleanup and a Complete Multi-Platform Run
summary: Eliware’s August 19 rolling run packaged upstream commit 787068def84c, validated six package lanes, and published twelve runtime images across EL10, Debian, and Ubuntu.
author: Eliware
content:
# Today’s GlusterFS Rolling Release: DHT Lock Cleanup and a Complete Multi-Platform Run

The August 19 Eliware rolling release followed upstream GlusterFS commit [`787068def84c`](https://github.com/gluster/glusterfs/commit/787068def84cb7b995ed69f1cd702ea05784aa8b). The upstream change, released as [DHT: unlock redirected migration on locked subvolume (#4703)](https://github.com/gluster/glusterfs/pull/4703), fixes a low-space migration path that could acquire an entry lock on one subvolume and later try to release it on another.

## What we packaged

The conductor completed all six package lanes successfully:

- EL10-compatible RPMs from the rolling `devel` source.
- Debian 12 (bookworm) DEBs from the same rolling source.
- Ubuntu 24.04 (noble) DEBs from the same rolling source.
- Stable package checkpoints for GlusterFS 11.2 were retained and reused.

The rolling package identifiers are:

```text
RPM: 2026.08.19-0.git787068def84c
DEB: 2026.08.19~rolling.g787068def84c-1
```

Each package lane passed its internal build smoke test, clean-target package smoke test, repository-integrity checks, provenance verification, signing, and publication checks.

## What images were published

The run published twelve runtime images in total: six rolling images from today’s commit and six previously validated stable 11.2 images reused through checkpoints. The six new rolling images are:

- `centos10-gluster:2026.08.19-787068def84c`
- `rocky10-gluster:2026.08.19-787068def84c`
- `alma10-gluster:2026.08.19-787068def84c`
- `oracle10-gluster:2026.08.19-787068def84c`
- `debian12-gluster:2026.08.19-787068def84c`
- `ubuntu24-gluster:2026.08.19-787068def84c`

The six stable 11.2 image lanes were retained and validated through checkpoints. Image checks covered installation, CLI availability, volume creation and mounting, file lifecycle operations, teardown, service shutdown, labels, package metadata, and provenance linkage.

## What we did not build

This was a rolling-source update, so there was no new upstream stable release and no new stable package generation. The existing stable 11.2 packages and images were reused through valid checkpoints.

We also did not build or validate a Fedora lane today. Fedora users can use the distribution’s own GlusterFS packages, but Fedora 44 is not currently one of this repository’s certified package or image targets. No builder base image was rebuilt because its inputs did not change.

## Evidence

The complete run record is available under run `20260819070652969-3fee9f22`. Its package provenance, image provenance, signed repository metadata, validation records, and release report are published alongside the artifacts.

Rolling builds are for evaluation and testing. They are clearly identified by their date-and-commit tag; use stable versions or immutable image digests when reproducibility and long-term support matter.
